description: Single source of truth for routing tunables shared by Python (services/transit/src/bledi_transit/domain/{tunables,fares}.py) and Rust (services/routing/src/{graph,router}.rs). Both sides hard-code these exact values; scripts/reconcile_tunables.py diffs them and fails the audit if they drift. See data/tunables_reconcile.json for the audit output.
pure_walk_rule: A pure-walk itinerary (no ride leg) longer than max_pure_walk_min minutes is only returned when no transit itinerary exists; if a transit candidate exists it wins. Direct point-to-point walk is only offered at <= max_direct_walk_m.

train.charging: base + per_km * km, charged once per boarding, capped

rail.charging: base + per_km * km, charged once per boarding, capped

louage.charging: base + per_km * km, charged once per boarding, capped

louaj.charging: base + per_km * km, charged once per boarding, capped

fare_notes: Fare is charged ONCE per boarding of a line (group consecutive legs on the same line), never per stop-pair edge. Charging per edge was the Rust bug that produced 69 DT Tunis->Sousse.
Caps: no single boarding costs more than cap_dt (train/rail 15 DT, louage/louaj 20 DT). Flat modes (bus/tram/metro/rural) are a flat ticket so the cap is a no-op.
Unknown modes are priced as bus (0.5 DT flat) on both sides.
Louage/louaj spelling: seed uses both; Python canonical_mode maps louage->louaj, Rust keeps both keys with identical values.
speed_notes: Louage/louaj highway cruising 90-110 km/h (100 km/h modelled average after stands/traffic); train avg 60 km/h as measured.
